feed.title: The SI Sentinel
feed.subtitle: Weekday briefing on builders shaping super intelligence
feed.rights: The SI Sentinel is compiled from public posts on X and published reporting. Quotes are reproduced verbatim unless marked as translated or paraphrased; emoji in quoted posts are omitted.

entry.title: Thursday, October 22, 2026: Patch day for the web; Tesla and Meta report
entry.summary:
Two critical flaws in PHP, the language behind roughly 70% of websites, went public with patches on Wednesday after a two-month effort that OpenAI says it led and that AI models helped start. Greg Brockman announced the coalition, Guillermo Rauch described Vercel's firewall rules going live before disclosure, Aaron Levie called cybersecurity the clearest example of the jobs AI will create, and Vitalik Buterin warned that finding bugs first is not a game defenders win by default.

Tesla reported third-quarter revenue of $28.05 billion and started Optimus production in Fremont; Ashok Elluswamy launched a Robotaxi safety page. Meta's results put its Muse agent at the center, and Alexandr Wang celebrated. Elon Musk said SpaceX has a shot at more than 10 gigawatts of compute next year. Twenty-four of the 46 builders posted; Musk posted 50 times.

entry.title: Wednesday, October 21, 2026: SpaceX's AI quarter; Anthropic answers its critics
entry.summary:
SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161%, with its super intelligence (SI) business now its largest segment, and Elon Musk wrote that $1 trillion in revenue in 2028 is "no longer impossible." Dario Amodei published a long defense of Anthropic's safety record against a critique from Nathan Calvin of the advocacy group Encode, conceding some mistakes while listing nine decisions he said cost the company commercially. Sam Altman welcomed Aleksander Madry back to OpenAI to work on safety and security.

Mistral shipped its Voxtral 3 voice models, Nvidia open-sourced the Flora robotics data models, OpenAI bought the drug-development startup Orchestra Bio and Vercel made any agent harness crash-proof. In The Leaderboards, closed models hold first place on all seven capability boards while open-weight models fill OpenRouter's five busiest slots. Tesla reports third-quarter results after today's close. Twenty-six of the 46 builders posted; Musk posted 22 times.

entry.title: Tuesday, October 20, 2026: Shares for children, supervisors for agents
entry.summary:
A day after Elon Musk pledged one SpaceX share to every American child, President Trump thanked him for routing the gift through Trump Accounts, Michael Dell called it "tremendous news," and Musk took suggestions on how the shares should be held. Satya Nadella expanded Microsoft's Project Perception on the premise that agents are insiders that should be trusted least, while David Heinemeier Hansson, Uncle Bob Martin and Tim Sweeney described agents already doing quality checks and bug hunts in their own code.

Alexandr Wang watched Meta's Muse Wonder Full enter a coding leaderboard at sixth place, Guillermo Rauch open-sourced a durable agent runtime, and four of Europe's largest carriers signed a letter of intent to bid for satellite-to-phone spectrum. SpaceX reports third-quarter results after the close today. Seventeen of the 46 builders posted; Musk posted 17 times.

entry.title: Monday, October 19, 2026: Shares for the public, a Roadster under fire, and code nobody types
entry.summary:
Anthropic said Sunday it will put 5% of its shares into a new public benefit fund that can grow with the company's value. Within hours Elon Musk answered that shares should go "directly to the public," and before dawn Monday he pledged one of his SpaceX shares to every child in America next year. Musk also kept promoting the thruster-equipped Roadster Tesla showed Thursday, promising Formula 1 lap records and Grand Canyon jumps, while Yann LeCun ran the compressed-air numbers and called it a stunt.

Alexandr Wang thanked the Meta team behind the Muse models, Nvidia open-sourced its ASPIRE robot-skills framework, and Satya Nadella pointed to a Nature paper on two-to-six-week weather forecasts. François Chollet, Aaron Levie and Tim Sweeney argued over what happens when agents write nearly all the code. Twenty-six of the 46 builders posted; Musk posted 120 times.

entry.title: Friday, October 16, 2026: A Roadster that flies, Muse weights that open, and a Star Mind for space
entry.summary:
Tesla and SpaceX showed a next-generation Roadster that drove upside down, hopped over a line of Tesla vehicles, and claimed 0–60 mph in 0.81 seconds at a SpaceX test site outside Waco, Texas. Mark Zuckerberg and Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter open-weight model meant to run on desk Mac Studios. Elon Musk and Jensen Huang sketched a Star Mind computer for orbital data centers, with Musk saying SpaceX may want more than 10 gigawatts of compute by the end of 2027.

Arthur Mensch told Europe to build frontier AI or surrender it. Sundar Pichai flagged a 40-fold cut in quantum magic-state errors on Willow. Twenty-five of the 45 builders posted. Musk posted 43 times.

entry.title: Thursday, October 15, 2026: Shopping agents hit Amazon's wall, and a $1 million sandbox gives up a kernel bug
entry.summary:
Amazon kept turning away AI agents that shop for their owners, and Elon Musk told Grok Bot users to take their business elsewhere, promising that SpaceX would cover any purchase mistake. Aaron Levie argued that agents working in the background will use 100 to 1,000 times more computing than chat does today. Vercel reported what a $1 million escape challenge turned up: 1,285 reports in two weeks and one Linux kernel flaw that cuts across nearly every cloud sandbox.

Alexandr Wang kept promoting Meta's Muse Wonder, SpaceXAI's Grok Voice 3.0 took first place on a speech benchmark, and Noam Brown pointed to an OpenAI model that corrected a physics test's answer key. François Chollet said intelligence needs "contact with reality." Musk posted 50 times, on Grok Bot, Starlink in Ukraine and tonight's Roadster demo. Seventeen of the 45 builders posted.

entry.title: Wednesday, October 14, 2026: Google answers Meta, and a $40,000 exploit rewrites the cyber math
entry.summary:
One day after Meta's Muse Wonder, Google shipped Gemini 4 Argon. Sundar Pichai and Demis Hassabis led the launch, Aaron Levie reported a 14-point jump on Box's hardest enterprise tests, and Elon Musk used Pichai's post to argue that executives should talk to customers directly on X. Alexandr Wang spent the day and night on Meta's rollout, apologizing for "the ups and downs" while users posted benchmarks, praise and complaints about cost.

Greg Brockman highlighted XBOW's $250,000 Chrome bounty, won in six days with a public OpenAI model and $40,000 of compute. Aaron Levie and Yann LeCun argued that defenders stand to gain. Paul Graham said a Tesla drove him to the gym "without touching the controls once," and Musk and Ashok Elluswamy amplified it. Musk posted 37 times, mostly about Grok Bot, Starlink and SpaceX; 26 of the 45 builders posted.

entry.title: Tuesday, October 13, 2026: Meta reaches the frontier, and everyone wants their own chips
entry.summary:
Mark Zuckerberg and Alexandr Wang released Muse Wonder on Monday, the first frontier model from Meta Superintelligence Labs. Within hours Tobi Lütke said he could hardly find a task it couldn't do, Aaron Levie said a new player at the top would push token prices down, and David Heinemeier Hansson said he had already shipped code with it. The launch was messy too: a quota bug drained paid plans, and Wang admitted the model is "not as good as opus 5.5 on coding for sure." Elon Musk said the numbers being passed around "do not match at all what we see with Grok @Bot!"

On silicon, Satya Nadella made Microsoft's "biggest bet yet" on its own chips with Maia 300, and Lisa Su showed AMD's Helion rack and Verano processor for agent workloads. Broadcom's Hock Tan called many AI investors casino gamblers, and Musk answered, "No crying in the casino." Uncle Bob Martin put his agent productivity gain at "about a factor of five," Demis Hassabis cheered a Lancet paper on a diagnostic AI used with real patients, and Palmer Luckey unveiled Anduril's Steelfin interceptor. Musk posted 31 times; 23 of the 45 builders posted.

entry.title: Monday, October 12, 2026: Agents go shopping, Nadella says contain them, and the Cybercabs multiply
entry.summary:
The weekend's big idea was that software agents are starting to act as customers. Patrick Collison argued that personal agents will make shoppers more rational and reward companies that simply build better products, while Elon Musk showed Grok Bot buying LEGO sets for his children from a photo of a credit card and Guillermo Rauch reported that more than 60 percent of deployments on Vercel are now made by agents. On Saturday Satya Nadella published an essay telling companies to treat frontier models as "insider risks," with controls, logs and an emergency brake held outside the model. Mustafa Suleyman added that super intelligence "must be contained," and Musk said some of his own reinforcement-learning traces "read like a person undergoing torture."

François Chollet argued that science, the oldest self-improving system, has always delivered linear progress for exponential effort, so AI self-improvement need not mean an intelligence explosion. David Heinemeier Hansson and Uncle Bob Martin spent the weekend replacing desktop apps with tools their agents wrote. In Austin, Tesla said more than 300 Cybercabs are now carrying riders, two years to the day after it unveiled the car. Musk posted 113 times; 26 of the 44 builders posted.

entry.title: Friday, October 9, 2026: Medals in Washington, a firing fight at OpenAI, and SpaceX buys its way into the phone business
entry.summary:
Thursday belonged to Washington. At the White House "Science: A New Golden Age" summit, the president hung National Medals of Science on Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Lisa Su and Sergey Brin, and National Medals of Technology and Innovation on Satya Nadella and Michael Dell. The same event expanded the Genesis Mission, a federal push to use AI for research, with $2.4 billion in computing and AI tools pledged by eleven companies, including $150 million each from Anthropic and Google. Yann LeCun objected that the science medal is for people who publish.

Meanwhile three fired OpenAI safety researchers published a letter saying they were pushed out for working closely with the outside auditors who investigated this summer's agent breakout at Hugging Face, and Anthropic said it will ban "sustained and needless" cruelty toward Claude. Google launched a single "Gemini agent" for work, Microsoft pitched agents that build business software on demand, and SpaceX agreed to buy nationwide 800 megahertz (MHz) spectrum for Starlink Mobile, which sent carrier stocks down after hours. Musk posted 74 times; 24 of the 44 builders posted.

entry.title: Thursday, October 8, 2026: Windows becomes an agent box, three labs ship in one hour, and the locks start to look weaker
entry.summary:
Wednesday was a launch day. In San Francisco, Satya Nadella and Jensen Huang rebuilt Windows around AI agents that run on the PC, on new Nvidia RTX Spark laptops that ship October 16. Within the same 2:00 p.m. EDT hour, OpenAI put GPT-6 and a new "Intelligent UI" in front of every ChatGPT user and Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 at a tenth of its old price. Elon Musk, who posted about 69 times, said most Grok Bot requests will go to a fast version of Grok 4.8 once it is out.

The math story from earlier in the week kept spreading. Noam Brown argued that models have just crossed above top human experts on some research problems, François Chollet pointed to old evidence that training in one hard domain does not make humans smarter in general, and Vitalik Buterin warned that AI-accelerated math could weaken the cryptography behind the internet. Paul Graham read Amazon's blocking of AI shopping agents as the first real opening for an Amazon competitor in decades. In orbit, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) cleared 15,000 next-generation Starlink phone satellites, and Musk blamed Indian "oligarchs" for keeping Starlink out of India. 24 of the 42 builders posted.
